causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Rebidding capacity to higher prices contributed to the 30-minute price exceeding $5,000/MWh.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: 980 MW of baseload capacity was unavailable on the day, all of which was planned since at least October 2021.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: There were planned outages to network equipment in NSW due to the upgrade of QNI which limited access to cheaper generation from NSW.

causes.label: fcas_co_optimisation
causes.quote: The price for 1.55 pm reached $11,073/MWh due to the trade off between the energy and FCAS markets with the high price of FCAS contributing to all but $37/MWh of the price.

causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Demand was higher than forecast and increased by around 700 MW between 1 pm and 2 pm driven by a change in rooftop solar output.

causes.label: solar_output
causes.quote: From around 1 pm rooftop solar output began to fall, increasing grid demand.

causes.label: ramp_rates
causes.quote: around 270 MW of generation with capacity priced below $5,000/MWh was unable to be dispatched because they could either not start generating in 5 minutes or were providing raise FCAS instead.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: limited imports over QNI from NSW to an average of 130 MW for the 2 pm 30-minute period compared to a usual 300-600 MW nominal limit.
